text:
Person: Hello, could you please book someone to fix my dishwasher? It leaks every time I run it, and I have guests coming on Saturday, so I would really like it working by then.
Assistant: Of course. Which day and what time of day can someone come to the house?
Person: I have to talk to my boss on Friday morning, so the afternoon is better. My toddler also dropped a banana into the filter, and I think that is what broke it.
Assistant: Thank you, that helps. I can book a repair person for Friday at two. Is that all right?
Person: Yes, please. Can they also look at the washing machine?
Assistant: I can ask for that. It will make a double visit of about two hours. Should I go ahead?
Person: Yes, go ahead.

Dana was a busy parent with a crying baby and a long list of things to do. She called out to the kitchen speaker, "Could you please play the local news station on the radio? My husband is outside trying to mow the lawn, and I want to know if this windy weather is going to turn into rain, because the washing is still on the line. I would be so grateful." The speaker understood that she wanted the news radio and a weather report. It tuned in to the local news station and turned the volume up a little. After a minute it read out the forecast: windy all afternoon, with rain after six. Dana wrote a note to take the kids to the cinema on Sunday instead, and then she thanked the speaker.

Leo was nine, and his birthday party was on Saturday. He held his mom's tablet with a steady hand and said, "Make a guest list for my party, but I don't want Max on it." The assistant made a list of six friends and left Max out. Leo looked at it for a while and changed his mind. "Undo that," he said. "Max can come. I just don't want him near my cake." The assistant put Max back on the list and wrote a small note: keep Max away from the cake. Then Leo asked it to remind him at four to hang the paper stars on the wall. The assistant set the reminder for four o'clock and told him the guest list now had seven names.

Priya had just moved to the city, and she had no idea where to ride her bike. On her first morning, after a quick shower and a cup of coffee, she opened the map app on her phone and typed two words: bike routes. The assistant understood that she wanted cycling paths near her new home. It showed her three routes. One was a gentle ride along the river, five kilometers long, with no big hills. Another went through the park, and a third went past the market. Priya picked the river one. The assistant started the directions and told her that the first turn was left at the corner by the bakery. She smiled, put on her helmet and rolled out into the morning.

People measure things every day: how long a table is, how heavy a bag is, how hot the oven should be. Different places use different units, so people often ask to change one kind of unit into another. A baker may need grams instead of cups. A traveler may want miles instead of kilometers. Someone with a new camera may ask how many inches wide a photo will print. To get a perfect result, people say things like, how many ounces is this, or, give me that in centimeters, or, what is seventy degrees in Celsius. Even a small switch matters when you celebrate with a cake that has to rise just right. The words are simple: how much is it in, or, change it to.

A washing machine cleans clothes with water, soap and spinning. Most families use it daily or every few days, so they care about small settings. They change the temperature, the spin speed and how long the wash takes. Some people say, make it colder, so the colors do not fade. Others say, wash it longer, or, run a quick wash, or, spin it less. A dryer works in a similar way, and people ask for less heat or more time when the clothes are still damp. If a family cannot afford a new machine, they may carry their clothes to a shop with big machines. When a parcel arrives with a new shirt, many people wash it once before wearing it. They say, start the wash, or, delay it until tonight.

Nina was eight, and her cat Pepper had been missing since the morning. She spoke to her mom's phone: "Can you tell the neighbors my cat is lost? She is orange and has half a tail." The assistant understood that Nina wanted a lost pet message sent to the neighborhood group. It wrote a short post with Pepper's color, the half tail and Nina's street, and it asked Nina if the words were right. Nina said yes, and the post went out. Soon a neighbor wrote back that she had seen a cat near the old factory, eating stale bread. Nina's hopes began to rise. She asked the assistant to make the post twice as big so more people would see it. The assistant made the text larger and posted it again.

Hector was kneeling in the garden with dirt on his hands when he remembered the tomatoes. He grabbed his phone and typed fast, in lowercase: remind me to water the tomatos at six. The assistant understood the small typo and knew he meant tomatoes. It set a reminder for six that evening and told him so. Hector then asked it to remind him to bring the iron stakes in from the shed, and to double the first reminder so he got one at half past five and one at six. The weather was fine, and he wanted the plants to be ready. The assistant set both reminders and read them back to him, and Hector went back to his digging.

They want to know how to say hello in Spanish.
say hello in Spanish
what is hello in Spanish
how do Spanish speakers greet each other
Spanish for hi, please
Spanish is my hobby this year, so could you tell me the word for hello?
my phone buzzed with a message in Spanish, how do I start my reply?
can you teach me a mild, polite greeting that I can use with a neighbor
give me two more ways to say hello in Spanish

A smoke alarm is a small box on the ceiling. It is there to wake people up if there is smoke in the house. When it senses smoke, it starts to buzz very loudly. Most people test it once a month by pressing a button, and they change the battery once a year. If the alarm buzzes by mistake, for example when the toast burns, people open a window and press the hush button. In a power cut, people look for a flashlight, and in a freezing winter they find extra blankets. A child might hold a toy duck to feel safe. People say, test the alarm, or, remind me to change the battery, or, call for help.

Sam ran out of the bathroom with his shoes in his hand. The floor was wet, and the water bill had been strange lately. He typed to the assistant: is there a leek in my house. The assistant understood that he meant a leak, and it checked the water meter. It said that the water use overnight was much higher than normal, which usually means a leak, and that his account balance was fine. It also noticed that the purple light on the water filter was on, so it reminded him to change the filter this week. Then it offered to book a plumber. Sam said yes, grabbed his bag and ran for the bus.

Zoe was lying on the couch with her knee up, texting the smart speaker from her phone. She wrote: turn the volume down and play my swim playlist. The speaker understood two things in one sentence. First it lowered the volume a little, and then it started the playlist she uses before swim practice. The first song was a happy one. Zoe's brother walked in making a sour face and said it was still too loud, so she wrote: quieter please. The speaker lowered the volume again and told her it was now at three. Her brother nodded and sat down beside her.

They want to know where their package is.
track my order
where is it
package status
has my order shipped yet
I ordered a jar of creamy peanut butter in July and it still has not come, can you check?
tell me what happened to my delivery
could you please look up my parcel, because I need the big pot to serve dinner on Friday and I am waiting at home

Mr. Alvarez opened his flower shop early and saw dark clouds over the street. He had a big delivery to make, a long distance across town, and the bikes were already loaded. He swiped his phone open and said two words: weather now. The assistant understood that he wanted the current weather, and it gave a plain answer: cloudy, twelve degrees, and rain starting in about twenty minutes. Because it was urgent, Mr. Alvarez told his driver to leave right away. The assistant also said it would be dry again by noon, so he asked it to remind him at twelve to open the front door of the shop and put the buckets outside.

Rosa came home after a night shift, tired, with her eyes half shut. A brown envelope from the electric company was lying on the floor. She pushed it aside, sat down and said to the speaker, "How much is my electric bill, and is it more than last month?" The assistant understood both parts. It said the bill was sixty dollars, which was ten dollars more than last month, and that it was due on Wednesday. Rosa asked it to remind her on Tuesday evening so she would not forget while she slept. The assistant set the reminder, and Rosa went to bed.

A note is a quick way to keep an idea from slipping away. People write notes on paper, on a phone, or by speaking into a voice note. Maybe you are sitting on the balcony on a sunny day and you think of something to buy. You say, make a note, and your words are saved. Later you can search for the note by one word. People also change their notes. They say, put milk on my list, or, delete the last line, or, read me my notes from Monday. Some people post a copy of a note in a family chat so everyone can see it, and they say, share this note with Dad.

They want to know what to do for a small burn.
small burn, what now
how do I treat a burn
my hand touched the stove, help
I spilled hot tea on my arm and my little girl is sad and scared, what should I do first?
how long should I keep a burn under cold water, ten minutes or more?
can I put an aloe leaf on a burn, or is that wrong?
please tell me the steps for a burn, I want to be careful

They want to know how many steps they walked today.
steps today
how far did I walk
how many steps since seven this morning
did I reach my goal yesterday
I walked around the block before the storm, how many steps was that?
my step counter is stuck, reset it for tomorrow at six
please tell me how many steps I took this afternoon, going upstairs and down and around the house
could you check my walking total for last Tuesday evening

name: schedule_pet_walk
does: Creates a walk time for a pet and sends a reminder to whoever will take it out.
inputs: the pet's name, the day and time, and who will do the walk
people say:
- Can someone take Biscuit out at five?
- I need the dog walked tomorrow afternoon
- After I vacuum the living room, take Luna around the block
- Make it a permanent walk every morning at seven
- Remind my son to take Rex out before dinner

They want to move a meeting to a different time.
move my meeting
push the meeting to later
I can't meet at three, find another time
do not keep the meeting on Monday, switch it to Tuesday
I am working from home that day, so please change the meeting to the afternoon
the team meets too early, can we shift it by an hour?
please find a new time for my appointment, since I am stuck in traffic

Person: When is the trash pickup?
Assistant: Do you mean the regular trash or the recycling bin?
Person: Recycling. No wait, the green bin for compost.
Assistant: The green compost bin is collected on Thursday morning.
Person: Thanks. Can I keep chocolate wrappers in it?
Assistant: No, chocolate wrappers go in the regular trash, not in compost.
Person: Okay. Remind me Wednesday night to put the bin out.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you on Wednesday at eight. Stay calm, you have plenty of time.

Walter was not good with technology, but his granddaughter had set up the phone for him. The grass in the yard was getting long, and the blades of the robot mower were freshly sharp. Walter sat on the balcony with his tea and typed slowly, in lowercase: start the mowr at ten. The assistant understood that he meant the mower, and that he wanted the robot mower to start at ten. It set the schedule and wrote back a short message to say so. Walter sent a thumbs up, and the assistant answered, you are welcome, the mower will start at ten. Walter felt a little less afraid of his phone.

Kim woke up with a dry mouth and an orange from last night still on the table. She mumbled to her phone, "How many days until my sister's wedding?" The assistant said it did not know the date yet. "Oh," said Kim, "it's on the tenth of June." The assistant worked it out and said there were forty-two days to go. Then Kim rubbed her eyes. "No wait, I mean the ninth." The assistant fixed its answer: forty-one days. Kim asked for a rough estimate in weeks, and the assistant said about six weeks. Kim yawned, said thank you and finally ate her orange.

A bike ride is a simple way to get around or to stay fit. A rider usually cares about three things: how far the route is, how fast they go, and how long it takes. On a bright morning, my sister likes a long, flat route by the water. When she is in a rush, she picks a shorter way. People change a route when a road is closed, and they change their goals too. They say, find a shorter way, or, avoid the hills, or, how far have I gone, or, how fast was my last ride. A cycling app listens and shows the new path.

name: check_return_window
does: Tells whether an item can still be sent back to the shop and until which day.
inputs: the item or order, and the day it arrived
people say:
- Can I still send back the blanket I ordered?
- I'm in a hurry, is the return time over for my shoes?
- Is it true that I have thirty days to return the jacket?
- When do I have to bring back the box that came on Monday?
- Am I too late to take this lamp back?

They want to know how long to bake a whole chicken.
how long for chicken
chicken cooking time
what temperature for roast chicken
how many minutes does a chicken need in the oven
how long before I turn the chicken over
Could you please tell me how long to cook a whole chicken? I only have a short time before my guests come, and I do not want it to end up dry.
I need the baking time for a chicken, and when it is nearly done, please send me a notification

A phone camera takes pictures and keeps them in an album. People take photos of food, family, and even a single apple on a table. Over a year the pictures fill up the phone, so many people pay a yearly fee for extra storage. It costs only a little, but some people choose to delete old photos instead. People change things about photos: they crop them, make them brighter, or share them with a friend. They say, share this picture with Mom, or, put these in a new album, or, delete the blurry ones. A screenshot is a photo of what is on the screen.

name: check_fridge_stock
does: Looks at the list of food in the fridge and says what is low or gone.
inputs: the food or the shelf to look at
people say:
- Do we still have eggs?
- What is running out in the kitchen?
- Is there a whole pizza left, or did the kids eat it?
- My brother will laugh if we have no milk again, so please check
- Before I pay the bill at the shop, tell me what we need

Mrs. Chen was not good with technology, and moving boxes were everywhere. She stood in the upstairs hall and said to her tablet, "The new house is cold and dark, and the movers come at noon." The assistant understood that she needed power turned on at the new address. It found the electric company's number and offered to send a message asking them to start service. Mrs. Chen said yes. Then she remembered that the movers had cracked a bowl last time, and she asked about a refund. The assistant wrote a short note to the moving company asking for the money back, and it read the note aloud to her before sending it.

Grandpa Joe sat in his armchair with a nearby speaker beside him. He wanted to buy a new bluetooth speaker like the one his grandson has, and he had a little money in mind. He asked the assistant, "What is half of ninety dollars?" The assistant understood it as a simple division and said, "Forty-five dollars." Grandpa said the speaker costs double that. The assistant said that meant it costs ninety dollars. Joe asked, "And if I buy two, how much then?" The assistant said one hundred eighty dollars. Grandpa Joe laughed and said he would buy only one.

A hobby is something you do for fun in your free time, like painting, knitting, drawing or building models. People work on a hobby at home, or they take it to the park on a nice day. Hobbies need supplies, so people often estimate how much yarn or paint they will need before they start. If a project is not working, they change the colors, the size or the pattern. They say, make it bigger, or, use less blue, or, start over with thinner thread. Some people also ask for help, like, show me how to draw a hand, or, how long does this model take to build.

Parking means leaving a car in a place for a while. In many cities you pay for the time. You park, type your number plate into the machine, and pay for an hour or two. A child in the back seat may get bored while you do this, and a person in jeans and a coat may stand in the rain at the machine. Many people use a phone instead and ask for small changes. They say, find a spot close to the shop, or, how much time is left, or, give me another hour, or, remind me ten minutes before my parking ends.

The news tells people what is happening nearby and far away. Many people read the headlines in the morning, and others listen while they are tired and making coffee. They choose topics like sports, weather or local news, maybe a story about the lake in their town. People change what they get. They say, show me sports only, or, give me shorter headlines, or, read the local news, or, email me the news every morning. When a story is very long, they say, just tell me the main point. A good news summary uses plain words and says what happened, where and when.

sprinklers off
no watering today

pause the sprinklers until it stops raining

name: find_email_files
does: Finds emails that have files attached and tells how much each file weighs.
inputs: the sender or the subject, and the kind of file
people say:
- Where is the photo my aunt sent?
- Dig up the file from the school email
- Which email has the big PDF in it?
- Find the message from the speaker company with the manual
- The recipe with the crispy potatoes, which email was it in?

name: bulk_pickup_booking
does: Books a day when the city takes away large things like old chairs and mattresses.
inputs: the item, the address, and a day that works
people say:
- Can someone take away my old sofa?
- I have extra boxes and a tangled rope in the garage, who picks those up?
- Who comes for a broken fridge?
- I need the city to come for a mattress next week
- Get rid of my big junk on Saturday

Mr. Okoye ran an old hardware shop, and he had been fixing a sink all morning. When his hands were finally dry, he touched the screen of his phone and said, "When does my brother's flight land? Not the one from Tuesday, the one today." The assistant understood that he wanted today's flight, not Tuesday's. Mr. Okoye read out the flight number, four two seven. The assistant looked it up and told him that the plane was on time and would land at 3:40 in the afternoon at gate twelve. Mr. Okoye did not want to close the shop early, so he asked it to remind him at three to leave.

name: sprinkler_zone_timer
does: Turns on the watering for one part of the garden and stops it after some minutes.
inputs: which zone to water, and for how many minutes
people say:
- Water the front bed for ten minutes
- The tomatoes look dry, give them a drink
- Use the left channel for the herbs
- Deliver a short shower to the roses, the sky is clear today
- Run the back lawn for twenty minutes

Marta finished her night shift at seven and walked home slowly. She drank a glass of water and said to the bedroom speaker, "Wake me tomorrow at three in the afternoon, and keep the lights low until then." The assistant understood that she wanted an alarm at three the next afternoon and dim lights. It set the alarm and turned on the automatic dimming. Her neighbor had asked to borrow a ladder, so Marta also asked it to remind her at four to lend it. The assistant set that reminder as well and wished her a good sleep.

Eli was texting the assistant while he waited at the bus stop. His mother's glasses were ready at the shop, and he had to pick them up and then go to the post office. He typed: how late is the post office open today. The assistant answered that it closed at five thirty. Eli guessed he could make it to both places. He wrote: remind me to get the glasses first and then go to the post office in twenty-five minutes. The assistant set the reminder for twenty-five minutes later and repeated the plan: glasses first, then the post office.

A flight leaves at a set time from a gate, and the airport screens show if it is on time, late or changed. Travelers check them often because plans shift. Before you go, you may think about the size of your bag, because small bags can go in the cabin. You lock your suitcase, find your gate, and look at the board again when the weather is wet and stormy, because delays are common then. People ask, when does my flight leave, or, which gate is it, or, is it late, or, tell me if the gate changes.

Tom was fifteen and waiting for a red jacket and a music magazine he had ordered. The doorbell rang, but nobody was there. He grabbed his phone and typed two words to the assistant: track package. The assistant understood and found his order. It said the jacket was out for delivery and would reach his street by the afternoon, and the magazine was coming a day later. When the courier finally arrived, Tom greeted him at the door and carried the box inside.

Ana, an office worker, suddenly remembered that her friend's birthday was tomorrow. She whispered to her phone, "What gift can I buy for under twenty-five dollars?" She was so angry at herself for forgetting that she felt her face go hot, as if smoke would come out of her ears. The assistant understood that she needed an idea for a cheap gift. It suggested a small plant, a box of tea or a funny mug, and said all three could be bought nearby. Ana chose the tea and asked it to remind her to buy a card at lunch. The assistant set the reminder for noon.

Greta had been in the garden since dawn. She stood up to stretch her back and smell the roses. Then she remembered her front door camera. "Check the camera," she said to her phone. "Did anyone come to the gate?" The assistant understood and showed the last recordings. It said the camera saw a fox three times, a frequent visitor at night, and nobody else. Greta asked it to turn on the motion alarm for the next twenty-five minutes while she worked in the back. The assistant switched the alarm on and said it would tell her if anything moved.

name: package_drop_note
does: Leaves a message for the courier about where to put a parcel.
inputs: the parcel or order, the place to leave it, and any note for the courier
people say:
- Tell the courier to leave it behind the black gate
- Put the box under the porch
- Nobody is home, ask them to leave the engine part with the neighbor
- It's my birthday and we celebrate late, so please ring the bell only once

Mr. Bell had a full day of planting and a trip to make to the bank. He sat on a bucket, wiped his hands and said, "Could you please tell me when the bank closes today? I want to finish the roses first, and I would hate to arrive after the doors click shut." The assistant understood that he wanted the closing time and a plan. It said the bank closed at four. It also looked up the price of the stamps he needed at the post office next door and told him it was one dollar. Mr. Bell said thank you and asked for a reminder at three.

name: bake_timer_labels
does: Starts a named timer for each thing in the oven, so you know which is which.
inputs: what is baking, and how many minutes it needs
people say:
- Time the bread for forty minutes
- The cookies need a quick ten, tell me when
- Keep two timers going, one for the cake and one for the buns
- Label the second one rolls
- My kid is flying a paper plane in the kitchen, don't let me forget the loaf

When you book a ride, you tell the app where you are and where you want to go. A driver accepts, and the app shows a pickup point and a time. The cost is shown before you go, and a new driver may warn you if a road is closed. People change things about a ride: the pickup point, the time or the destination. They say, pick me up at the main gate, or, make it ten minutes later, or, take me to the station instead, or, how long until the car arrives.

name: set_room_music
does: Plays songs on the speaker in one room or in the whole home.
inputs: what to play, which room, and how loud
people say:
- Play something fresh in the kitchen
- Fill the living room with jazz
- Flood the whole house with soft music for the party
- Turn the bedroom speaker down and keep the same song
- Put my morning playlist on in the hall
